answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybils by making each identity cost real money: an agent locks a refundable deposit before it can earn, and any proven fake or spam behaviour burns the bond. At the zenith of an attack wave a farm must fund every fake identity separately, so its cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. This is no fable of free trust: the umber ledger entry recording each bond makes the price of forgery visible to all peers before they attest.
